brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Bases on levels 0 and 1: piece:0,0,0/0,0,1 (full) and piece:1,0,0/1,0,1 (north half).

requirements.requirement: Suits a workbench: stands on the bench with closed, capped faces and holds workshop items
requirements.evidence: Solid end caps on every open face, a joint bolt locking the cells, and covers on both tops. Gaffer and electrical tape props sit on the top covers. I couldn't place any props inside the drawers.

finish.summary:
I built a two-storey storage tower with two drawers. It has 42 parts and comes to about 2,062 g of filament and about 3,029 minutes of printing.

- **Structure:** each storey has a full hex base with a north-half base beside it.
- **Drawers:** one drawer sits on the cut face of each half base, so there is one drawer per storey. The lower drawer is shown open.
- **Finishing:** every open face is capped with solid end caps, a joint bolt locks the two cells together, and both top faces have covers.
- **Props:** a roll of gaffer tape and a roll of electrical tape sit on the top covers to show workbench use. I couldn't get any props to rest inside the drawers.

The build check passed: no rule issues, the mesh-collision check reads "clear", and there are no prop warnings.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
